lesson_title: Simple vs Compound: The R60,17 the Bank Didn't Mention
hook_text: Same R4 000. Same 7%. Two different answers, R60,17 apart. Who earned the extra?
clip_script: Year one: 7 percent of 4 000 is R280, exactly as before. But now the move that changes everything: the R280 does not sit outside the deal — it JOINS the balance. You now have R4 280 working for you. Year two: 7 percent of 4 280 — not of 4 000 — which is R299,60. Spot the extra R19,60? That is interest earned by last year's R280. The interest hatched. New balance: R4 579,60. Year three: 7 percent of 4 579,60 is R320,57. Balance: R4 900,17. Set the two finals side by side: R4 840 the bicycle way, R4 900,17 the hen-coop way. The R60,17 difference is not a trick — you watched it arrive in pieces.
visual_style: Split screen: a bicycle with a flat R280 tag dropping in each year on one side; on the other, eggs hatching into hens whose new eggs hatch again, with a running rand counter accelerating above the coop.
pacing: Year-by-year beat, hold on the R19,60 reveal, quick-fire side-by-side totals to finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master both growth formulas.
